verses.text: Then I looked, and there was the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, with 144,000 people who had his name and his Father’s name written on their foreheads.
I heard a sound from heaven like the roar of rushing waters and a loud peal of thunder. The sound I heard was like harpists playing their harps.
They sang a new song before the throne, the four living creatures, and the elders. No one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been bought from the earth.
These are the ones who didn’t defile themselves with women, for they remained virgins. They follow the Lamb wherever he goes. They were bought from among humanity as firstfruits for God and the Lamb.
No lie was found in their mouths; they’re blameless.
Then I saw another angel flying high overhead, carrying the eternal good news to announce to those who live on earth—to every nation, tribe, language, and people.
He called out loudly, “Fear God and give him glory, because the hour of his judgment has come. Worship the one who made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and the springs of water.”
A second angel followed and said, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the Great, which made all the nations drink the wine of her passionate immorality.”
A third angel followed them and said loudly, “If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives its mark on their forehead or hand,
they’ll drink the wine of God’s fury, poured full strength into the cup of his anger. They’ll be tormented with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels and the Lamb.
The smoke of their torment rises forever and ever. There’s no rest day or night for those who worship the beast and its image or anyone who receives the mark of its name.”
This calls for endurance from God’s holy people, who keep his commands and remain faithful to Jesus.
Then I heard a voice from heaven say, “Write this: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “they’ll rest from their labor, because their deeds follow them.”
Then I looked, and there was a white cloud, and seated on the cloud was someone like a son of man, with a gold crown on his head and a sharp sickle in his hand.
Another angel came out of the temple and called loudly to the one seated on the cloud, “Take your sickle and reap, because the time to reap has come. The harvest of the earth is ripe.”
So the one seated on the cloud swung his sickle over the earth, and the earth was harvested.
Another angel came out of the temple in heaven, and he too had a sharp sickle.

Then another angel, who had authority over the fire, came from the altar and called loudly to the angel with the sharp sickle, “Take your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of grapes from the earth’s vine, because its grapes are ripe.”
The angel swung his sickle over the earth and gathered its grapes, throwing them into the great winepress of God’s anger.
The winepress was trampled outside the city, and blood flowed out from it, rising as high as horses’ bridles for a distance of about 180 miles.
